title: A Tale of Two Geometries: Adaptive Optimizers and Non-Euclidean Descent
claim: A norm can be seen as the supremum of a family of simpler primal norms and, dually, the infimum of dual norms.
layout: 2 panels side-by-side, primal then dual, nested colored ellipses inside black square
description: Two side-by-side 2-D plots with grid lines. The left panel has axes x1 and x2 from -2.5 to 2.5. A bold black unit square, the l-infinity ball, sits at the center. Five colored, translucent ellipses (orange, red, purple, blue, green) with differing aspect ratios all touch the square's corners and enclose it, so the square is their intersection. The right panel has axes g1 and g2 from -1.5 to 1.5. A black dashed diamond, the l1 ball, is filled by dashed ellipses in the same colors. Each ellipse touches the diamond at its vertices or edges, so the diamond is their union. The eye goes first to the central square and diamond, then to the colored ellipses. There is no text beyond the axis labels.
caption:
Here we demonstrate the duality between the supremum of the primal norms and the infimum of the corresponding dual norms for any well-structured preconditioner set $\cH$. In particular, we consider $\cH=\{all diagonal PSD matrices\}$, in which case $
orm{\cdot}_\cH=
orm{\cdot}_\infty$ and $
orm{\cdot}_{\cH,*}=
orm{\cdot}_1$. Left figure: the $\|\cdot\|_\infty$-unit ball (black square) in the primal space is the intersection of all $\|\cdot\|_ H$-unit ball (colored ellipses) for $ H\in\cH$ with $\Tr( H)\leq 1$, that is, $\|\cdot\|_\infty$ is the supremum of all such primal $\|\cdot\|_ H$ norms. Right figure: the $\|\cdot\|_1$-unit ball (dashed black square) in the dual space is the union of all $\|\cdot\|_{ H,*}$-unit balls (dashed ellipses) for $ H\in\cH$ with $\Tr( H)\leq 1$, that is, $\|\cdot\|_1$ is the infimum of all such dual $\|\cdot\|_{ H,*}$ norms.
abstract: Adaptive optimizers can reduce to normalized steepest descent (NSD) when only adapting to the current gradient, suggesting a close connection between the two algorithmic families. A key distinction between their analyses, however, lies in the geometries, e.g., smoothness notions, they rely on. In the convex setting, adaptive optimizers are governed by a stronger adaptive smoothness condition, while NSD relies on the standard notion of smoothness. We extend the theory of adaptive smoothness to the nonconvex setting and show that it precisely characterizes the convergence of adaptive optimizers. Moreover, we establish that adaptive smoothness enables acceleration of adaptive optimizers with Nesterov momentum in the convex setting, a guarantee unattainable under standard smoothness for certain non-Euclidean geometry. We further develop an analogous comparison for stochastic optimization by introducing adaptive gradient variance, which parallels adaptive smoothness and leads to dimension-free convergence guarantees that cannot be achieved under standard gradient variance for certain non-Euclidean geometry.
